classification.difficultyReason: Infer the radius from total height minus cone height, recognise that the shared circle is internal, and combine cone and hemisphere curved areas while retaining an exact multiple of π.

content.prompt: A water buoy is in the shape shown. Find the surface area, in exact form.

spec.description: Unshaded upright cone joined to a lower hemisphere. Ordinary outlines and labels use black. Red dashed construction marks retain the source distinction. All three supplied measurements, the altitude leader, centre dot and right-side total-height dimension are retained.
spec.mathematics: The cone and hemisphere share a circular radius. Cone perpendicular height is 36 cm, cone slant height is 39 cm and total height is 51 cm. Drawing coordinates use the dimensionless ratio r:h = 15:36. Cone silhouette endpoints are derived from tangency to the projected joining ellipse.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the radius and surface area are withheld.

answer.worked:
The hemisphere's height equals its radius.
$$\begin{align*}
r &= 51-36\\
  &= 15\ \mathrm{cm}\\
A &= \pi rl+2\pi r^2\\
  &= \pi(15)(39)+2\pi(15)^2\\
  &= 585\pi+450\pi\\
  &= 1035\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
The supplied slant height is consistent: $15^2+36^2=39^2$. The shared circular face is internal, so it is excluded.
